Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the capability looks promising for our real-time personalization flows. Procurement asked me to consolidate a short list of technical commitments we need to see before we can move to a pilot. Specifically they're asking about latency SLOs for the hosted API (p50/p95 targets), how you measure them (measurement windows, aggregation rules), and what operational evidence you can share to make this auditable to our infra team.

Can you confirm:
- The default p50/p95 target values you commit to for hosted customers in the US region
- The measurement window (rolling vs fixed epoch) and sampling strategy used for the contract
- Whether you can provide a snapshot of a four-week telemetry sample and an annotated playbook describing transient carveouts (maintenance, regional bursts)

Procurement has asked for an evidence package they can attach to the contract review. Would appreciate a short delivery timeline — ideally by EOD Tuesday so they can include it in the SOW draft.

Thanks,

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. We've pulled together a concise evidence package and a proposed measurement plan; high level answers below, details/attachments attached.

Quick answers:
- Standard hosted commitments (US region): p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 320ms for text-generation routes on our small/medium model tier. We publish per-model performance profiles; committed values can be tailored by plan.
- Measurement: rolling 5-minute window aggregated into hourly buckets for contract reporting; we also compute a rolling 24-hour derived view for operational insights. Aggregation excludes synthetic maintenance windows and scheduled orchestration events (these are documented in the playbook).
- Evidence: included a 4-week telemetry snapshot (p50/p95 per hour), a sampling manifest (how traces were sampled), and our Measurement Playbook that describes carveouts, synthetic probe methodology, and audit steps.

Attachments: measurement-playbook.pdf (playbook), p95-sample-snapshot.csv (four-week hourly snaps), orion-evidence-20261130.zip (raw extracts + query scripts).

I'll let Ben add a bit more on how we compute p95 and what telemetry consumers should expect. If Procurement needs additional proof (SOC2 audit extracts, tracer IDs), we can point them to the audit folder in the shared drive.

Next steps:
- Ben: can you add the extract notes and the recommended contract clause wording for rolling windows?
- Lauren: legal/terms — any constraints we should call out for hosted commitments vs dedicated?

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0500
Subject: Technical notes: p50/p95 computation and measurement windows

Team — technical summary to include in the evidence package and contract appendix. Please review for accuracy.

Computation rules (summary):
- Raw telemetry: each request record includes timestamp, region, model_id, route, latency_ms (end-to-end server-side), route_tags (streaming/batched), cache_hit boolean, and request_id.
- Sampling: production telemetry is sampled at request level with priority sampling for large customers; the sample manifest included in the zip maps sampling rates by route and hour. For contract reporting we reconstruct population percentiles using Horvitz–Thompson weighting to correct for sampling bias.
- Aggregation windows: we compute percentiles in rolling 5-minute windows (non-overlapping) and then summarize those windows into hourly and daily reports. Contract language references the hourly summary (each hour contains up to twelve 5-minute windows) as the authoritative measurement.
- p50/p95 targets: default p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 320ms (US hosted, text-gen small/medium). If the customer wants a stricter commitment we can include a dedicated tier or model pinning clause.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows and confirmed cloud provider incidents are excluded. We also provide a documented transient-burst carveout for traffic spikes caused by customer-side traffic bursts (requires mutual action plan and evidence).
- Evidence package contents: four-week hourly snapshots, sample manifest, query scripts, synthetic probe results, and an annotated list of outlier events. We provide CSV extracts and a reproducible notebook to run the aggregation queries.

Contract clause (suggested wording excerpt):
"Latency measurements for the hosted API shall be calculated from Redwood's server-side telemetry using rolling five-minute measurement windows aggregated into hourly summaries. For each contracted hour, Redwood will compute the p50 and p95 latencies for the customer's traffic for specified routes. The parties agree that scheduled maintenance windows and documented cloud provider incidents (mutually acknowledged) will be excluded from contractual calculations. Sampling bias will be corrected via Horvitz–Thompson weighting as documented in the Measurement Playbook."

--- end forwarded content ---

I attached the scripts and the CSV to the drive link. My recommended turnaround to deliver the full audit bundle to Orion is EOD Wednesday (two business days from Maya's ask) — that gives us time to confirm sampling manifests and scrub any sensitive request IDs.
